question: In the treatment of heart failure:

options.opa: Angiotensin receptor blockers (ARA II) have shown superiority over angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors and should be the first therapeutic option.
options.opb: Aldosterone antagonists have not shown prognostic improvement, being contraindicated in patients with advanced systolic dysfunction and functional grade IV.
options.opc: Beta-blockers have been shown to decrease mortality in patients with decreased ejection fraction.
options.opd: Cardiac resynchronization pacemaker therapy is indicated in patients with systolic dysfunction whenever the QRS is narrow (less than 120 msg).
options.ope: The implantation of automatic defibrillators is contraindicated in patients with ventricular dysfunction, especially if it is caused by ischemia.

enhanced_information: In the treatment of heart failure: Angiotensin receptor blockers (ARA II) may be superior to ACE inhibitors and could be considered as the first therapeutic option. Aldosterone antagonists have not shown prognostic improvement and are contraindicated in patients with advanced systolic dysfunction and functional grade IV. Beta-blockers have been shown to decrease mortality in patients with decreased ejection fraction. Cardiac resynchronization pacemaker therapy is indicated in patients with systolic dysfunction when the QRS is narrow (less than 120 ms). The implantation of automatic defibrillators is contraindicated in patients with ventricular dysfunction, especially if it is caused by ischemia.
analysis: In the treatment of heart failure, the core medical principle is to optimize therapies that have shown to improve outcomes and reduce mortality. Based on consensus and enhanced information, the most likely correct options are that beta-blockers have been shown to decrease mortality in patients with decreased ejection fraction, and cardiac resynchronization pacemaker therapy is indicated in patients with systolic dysfunction when the QRS is narrow (less than 120 ms). Angiotensin receptor blockers (ARA II) may be considered as a first therapeutic option over ACE inhibitors, but the superiority is not definitive. Aldosterone antagonists have not shown prognostic improvement and are contraindicated in certain patients. The implantation of automatic defibrillators is not contraindicated in all patients with ventricular dysfunction, especially if it is caused by ischemia.
